Jhoka struggled with the long hose, her jumpsuit marked with long, greasy lines from the hose rubbing against her as she pulled it further and further. Ahead of her was yet more hose and an uncomfortable metal box with a strap so it could be more easily carried but she wasn't sure what creature would have found such a contraption comfortable. Every movement banged against her thick, tough hide that wasn't used to repeated assaults and her scales were starting to get damaged from the abuse; a sharp throbbing pain had developed where her muscles were most bruised from the sharp edges.

"So this is life among the stars?" she snapped out finally, huffing with frustration as she gave one final yank before throwing herself down on the muddy ground. "I am still on the ground, pulling this.. this... whatever it is called! I hate this!"

Slowly she picked herself up and grabbed the metal box by it's strap and holding it with both hands to avoid discomfort. After almost fifteen minutes of walking she realized her feet were sinking deep enough into the mud to produce puddles of water in the prints which was a good sign. Yesterday she had enjoyed herself as she settled into her new home, the room at the very rear of the ship was a temporary spot for her but soon she would have her own bed in the children's room. This arrangement worked out well for the young tribal girl, she didn't want to sleep alone and she had insisted that she could be trusted to care for the toddlers given her previous experiences. Most of her youth had been spent trying, and failing, to impress her mother who had extremely little patience for children or even much of a bond with her daughter. Often she was left behind while the other hunters left to look after the young which seemed to happen more and more often as Jhoka got older.

What was most disappointing was she came from perfect stock, her father was almost legendary among all the clan hunters and her mother was a renowned warrior who had proven herself in combat many times. Unfortunately for Jhoka her species sometimes went through severe post-partum depression that often ended in total abandonment of the child, she was one of the unlucky ones to be rejected by her mother. Many learned to love their children anyway, but she was only kept around because her father did not have the hormonal imbalance necessary to reject her. He immediately fell in love with his baby daughter, her mother only humored her mate simply because she loved him that much.

Inzili's tribe would have had the young Jhoka raised by the community since affection for children and male mates was unimportant in their society. Thankfully that way of life had been all but eradicated: the rigid societies that formed around it were incapable of dealing with the violent humans. Humans didn't care about "fighting with honor" and simply slaughtered any native who got in their way and enslaved those who survived, after they left they had forever changed the natives.

Jhoka's constant failures and disappointments had given her an uncanny endurance for adversity and she didn't shy away from challenges, even if she was completely terrified about enduring them. What her clan saw as traits unfit for a warrior, automatically pushing her down to a lower social status, her new employer saw as untapped potential. Had she been somehow transported two hundred years in the past and to Stan's training battalion the instructors there would have worked her, beat her, and finally broken her but they would have built her up into something magnificent. She couldn't have known that, as far as she was concerned the Goddess had remembered to smile down at her after forgetting for so long. Even if that weren't true she didn't want to quit the new challenge, she felt like she might have a chance at success in the new setting and she carried onward.

That undaunted perseverance served Jhoka every day and soon she was at her destination: a shallow river with a wide floodplain. Remembering her instructions was simple enough, take the hose and screw it into the metal box, flip the switch and then throw it as far as she could into the water. Stan told her she could even swing it gently by the hose if she so desired and she did exactly that, the box flying just beyond the center of the river with a loud splash.

Walking back was far easier, she didn't have to stop and backtrack to pull the middle part of the hose several times and she followed the long, plastic snake on her long trek back.

Before she had left on her journey she had made her first mistake, unlike her kind it was customary to be clothed when in the presence of others and her attempts to engage the human in conversation were thwarted. This rule didn't make any sense to her, he had disrobed her already and knew what she looked like and even if he didn't it wasn't like she was particularly unique. Obviously he had seen nude females before, the evidence of that fact had been left in their cribs by the time she left.

Fortunately it wasn't a very big rule and she had only received a gentle chiding for it, but it gave her an opportunity to choose new clothes! Or actually Inzili's old clothes that didn't fit very well, every time she walked it reminded her that the purple matriarch of the ship had longer legs, a more muscular torso, and a slightly slimmer tail than Jhoka did and the jumpsuit had a habit of pinching in all sorts of wrong places. At least it was mostly too big, but she was still forced to wear the clothing underneath that, as much as she didn't want to admit it, felt surprisingly comfortable. Apparently they were disposable though, tawaunan scales were not kind on the soft fabric. There was an option for footwear that, oddly, covered the entire foot but Jhoka already had a pair of good footwraps that protected the already tough pads meant for traction.

Suddenly her instincts told her to look around.

For a moment she almost forgot where she was, the river's floodplain was far behind her and had been out of sight for a long time. Jhoka's eyes scanned the trees all around her carefully, but she couldn't see anything that would have provoked alarm.

"I wonder why I feel so uncomfortable," she said to herself.

Experience had taught her never to doubt her instincts, many others like her had fallen victim to the local wildlife or were simply never found after failing to return for a few days. They would still get their funeral pyre, but it would be loaded with only their possessions and a cloth sack filled with blessed cuts of meat, sand, and a clay mask. Just thinking of that type of send-off made her shudder, it wasn't shameful or dishonorable but it was... hollow, it felt hollow; the inadequate sensation of not seeing a body being sent off to the sky lingered for days. Not her, the human had given her a special box that sent her voice to him when the button was pressed; he had made sure she knew how it worked.

That uneasy feeling made her hand find it, to make sure it was there, if she needed help in the wilderness he could follow the artificial snake she had placed right to her.

Movement in the corner of her eye made her scales curl up.

Far off in the distance she saw seven warriors painted bright red with white stripes, and judging by their quick movements to close the distance as silently as possible they had already spotted her. They had made a crucial mistake early in their pursuit, besides being painted red and white of course, taking the high and easy route to cover the distance rather than hiding in the lower dips of the terrain. These were not hunters, not like Jhoka was, they didn't stalk for food but instead only stalked to get close.

Fortunately she had an advantage there, they didn't and knew safety was within distance of a hard run.
